comparison.objective: Candidate commissions and locks a robot-axis shock absorber through dynamic impact trials; pr-1450 clamps a glued wood panel flat with alternating clamps.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed hex-key engagement, setscrew release/retightening, fine collar rotation, and response-guided adjustment. pr-1450 requires placing a clamp across a panel and closing three sliding jaws with controlled clamping force.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two safe physical cycles within energy, velocity, stroke, rebound, overload, hard-stop, and drift limits. pr-1450 requires a closed, level joint with three alternating clamps at 1–6 N and fails above 6 N.
comparison.reason: Force control and bimanual handling are generic shared primitives, but the tested abilities differ: dynamic damper tuning and retention versus spatial clamp arrangement and distributed panel compression. Candidate rubric still lacks numeric thresholds for collar drift, excessive rebound, overload, locking torque, and thread damage; these omissions do not make this unrelated objective a plausible duplicate.
